name: CureBench
intro: CURE-Bench 是 NeurIPS 2025 治疗推理竞赛基准，评测模型在药物决策、治疗规划、安全性与疗效分析中的多步推理、工具使用和临床可靠性。
build_method: 基于 TxAgent 数据生成系统，以 QuestionGen、TraceGen、ToolGen 三个模块生成并验证临床问题、推理轨迹和工具解法
metric: 正确性、鲁棒性、效率、事实性与临床相关性的预定义加权总分；头部提交由人类专家复核
eval_feature: 内部知识赛道与工具增强赛道；智能体裁判和临床专家验证
scale: 数千条（精确数量未公开）
build_method_en: Use a TxAgent-based modular pipeline—QuestionGen, TraceGen, and ToolGen—to generate and validate clinical questions, reasoning traces, and tool-based solutions
eval_feature_en: Internal-knowledge and tool-augmented tracks with agentic judges and clinical-expert validation
intro_en: CURE-Bench is a NeurIPS 2025 therapeutic-reasoning competition benchmark for multi-step drug decision-making, treatment planning, safety and efficacy analysis, tool use, and clinical reliability.
metric_en: Predefined weighted aggregate of correctness, robustness, efficiency, factuality, and clinical relevance, with human-expert review of top submissions
drawio_review_note: Aligned with the official CURE-Bench site and NeurIPS 2025 competition abstract. CURE-Bench covers twelve published therapeutic task families spanning treatment recommendation, adverse events, drug labeling and ingredients, warnings, dependence, dosage, special populations, pharmacology, clinical information, nonclinical toxicology, and patient information. Its validated TxAgent-derived multi-agent pipeline is documented as QuestionGen for clinically plausible queries, TraceGen for grounded multi-step reasoning traces, and ToolGen for callable biomedical tools; the output is described only as thousands of examples, so no exact item count is claimed. Track 1 permits internal model knowledge only, while Track 2 permits external biomedical tools and real-time information. Submissions include reasoning traces, final answers, token use, and model metadata. The official evaluation combines correctness, rephrasing and option-order robustness, token/tool efficiency, agentic factuality and clinical-relevance checks, plus expert assessment of top submissions into a predefined weighted score. Exact task instances, split sizes, metric weights, prompts, and judge configuration are not publicly specified, and the diagram preserves those boundaries.
